scenarios.title: Motion along a line
scenarios.description: A particle moving in one dimension under any mix of forces.
scenarios.law: Newton's second law along the line: mass times acceleration equals the sum of the forces.

fields.label: Constant acceleration
fields.hint: Enter it directly, or let it follow from the forces switched on.

fields.label: Angle of the incline
fields.hint: 0° is a level surface; x points up the slope.

fields.label: Time until it stops (or turns round)
Position where it stops (greatest height when thrown up)
Energy removed by drag and friction

effects.label: Gravity
effects.description: The weight, acting straight down or along a slope.

effects.label: Applied force
effects.description: A constant push or pull along the line.

effects.label: Sliding friction
effects.description: μN against the motion; it can hold the object still.

effects.label: Air resistance
effects.description: A force opposing the motion that grows with speed.

effects.label: Spring
effects.description: A restoring force -kx towards x = 0 (Hooke's law).

effects.label: Buoyancy
effects.description: The surrounding fluid pushes up with the weight of the fluid displaced.

effects.label: Driving force
effects.description: A periodic push, F₀ cos(ωt).

effects.label: Gravity weakens with height
effects.description: Inverse-square gravity, for very high drops.

presets.label: Car accelerating
presets.description: From rest to 27 m/s in 6 s: the acceleration and the distance.

presets.label: Ball thrown upward
presets.description: A ball thrown up at 20 m/s from a 1.5 m hand, no air resistance.

presets.label: Skydiver
presets.description: An 80 kg skydiver, belly to earth, jumping from 4000 m.

presets.label: Dropped baseball
presets.description: A baseball dropped from a 50 m tower; where is it after 2 s?

presets.label: Raindrop
presets.description: A raindrop is seen to fall at 6.5 m/s: what is its drag coefficient c?

presets.label: Fog droplet
presets.description: A 20 µm droplet, slow enough for linear (Stokes) drag.

presets.label: Car braking
presets.description: A car at 25 m/s brakes on a level road with μ = 0.7: how far does it go?

presets.label: Block sliding down a ramp
presets.description: Released 2 m up a 30° ramp with μ = 0.2.

presets.label: Crate pushed across a floor
presets.description: A 20 kg crate pushed with 120 N against friction μ = 0.4 for 3 s.

presets.label: Car suspension
presets.description: One corner of a car (400 kg) pushed down 5 cm and released: where is it after 0.3 s?

presets.label: Door closer
presets.description: What damping makes a 30 kg door on a 60 N/m closer shut without bouncing (ζ = 1)?

presets.label: Lab cart on a spring
presets.description: A cart on a spring is timed at 1.0 s per swing: what is the spring constant?

presets.label: Washing machine
presets.description: A 60 kg drum on its mounts, shaken by an unbalanced load at 5 Hz.

presets.label: Hanging scale
presets.description: A 2 kg bag stretches a spring scale 4 cm: what is k, and how fast does it bob?

scenarios.title: Motion in a plane
scenarios.description: A particle moving in two dimensions: projectiles, charges in fields, orbits.
scenarios.law: Newton's second law in two dimensions: mass times acceleration equals the sum of the forces.

fields.label: Gravity
fields.hint: 9.81 m/s² at the Earth's surface; it acts in the -y direction.

fields.label: Gravitational parameter of the central body
Initial direction above the x axis
Initial velocity along x
fields.hint: Give the speed and direction, or the two components; either is enough.

fields.label: Velocity along x at that time
Velocity along y at that time
Escape speed from the starting point

effects.label: Uniform gravity
effects.description: A constant downward acceleration g.

effects.label: Air resistance
effects.description: A force opposing the velocity through the air.

effects.label: Wind
effects.description: The air itself moves along x, so drag acts on the velocity relative to it.

effects.label: Electric field
effects.description: A uniform field E pushes a charge q with force qE.

effects.label: Magnetic field
effects.description: A uniform field out of the plane turns a moving charge: force qv×B.

effects.label: Central attraction
effects.description: Inverse-square attraction towards the origin, as for an orbit.

presets.label: Free kick
presets.description: A ball kicked at 25 m/s, 30 degrees above the ground.

presets.label: Golf drive
presets.description: A 45.9 g ball leaving at 70 m/s and 12 degrees, with air resistance.

presets.label: Basketball free throw
presets.description: Released at 7.3 m/s from 2.1 m up; the hoop is 4.19 m away and 3.05 m high.

presets.label: Long jump
presets.description: A take-off speed of 9.5 m/s and a jump of 8.0 m: the take-off angle?

presets.label: Javelin in a headwind
presets.description: An 800 g javelin thrown at 28 m/s and 36 degrees into a 5 m/s headwind.

presets.label: Electron in a magnetic field
presets.description: An electron moving at 10⁶ m/s across a 1 mT field.

presets.label: Electron between deflection plates
presets.description: An electron at 2×10⁷ m/s crossing a 5 kV/m field for 2 ns.

presets.label: Satellite in low orbit
presets.description: 400 km above the Earth, moving at 7.673 km/s at right angles to the radius.

presets.label: Transfer orbit
presets.description: From 6678 km with 10.25 km/s: how far out does it go?

scenarios.title: Rotation and pendulums
scenarios.description: Turning about a fixed axis: Iθ'' = sum of torques. Pendulums, torsion springs, flywheels.
scenarios.law: Newton's second law for rotation: moment of inertia times angular acceleration equals the net torque.

fields.label: Moment of inertia about the axis
Distance from the pivot to the centre of mass
Rotational kinetic energy at that time
Speed at the bottom of the swing

effects.label: Gravity
effects.description: A weight hanging from the pivot pulls the system back to the vertical.

effects.label: Large angles
effects.description: Use sin θ exactly instead of the small-angle approximation.

effects.label: Torsion spring
effects.description: A restoring torque proportional to the angle.

effects.label: Damping
effects.description: A torque opposing the rotation, proportional to the angular velocity.

effects.label: Applied torque
effects.description: A constant torque about the axis.

presets.label: Grandfather clock
presets.description: A pendulum that swings once every two seconds: how long is it?

presets.label: Playground swing
presets.description: A 2.5 m swing released from 60 degrees.

presets.label: Foucault pendulum
presets.description: A 67 m pendulum released from 3 degrees.

presets.label: Damped lab pendulum
presets.description: A 0.5 m pendulum with damping rate 0.1 per second, after 10 s.

presets.label: Measuring gravity
presets.description: A 1 m pendulum has a period of 2.007 s: what is g?

presets.label: Swinging metre stick
presets.description: A 150 g metre stick pivoted at one end (I = mL²/3).

presets.label: Flywheel spinning up
presets.description: A 0.5 kg·m² flywheel driven by 2 N·m from rest for 10 s.

presets.label: Wheel coasting down
presets.description: A wheel at 300 rpm slows with damping rate 0.2 per second: its speed after 5 s?

presets.label: Torsion pendulum
presets.description: A disc of 0.002 kg·m² on a wire twists with a 1.5 s period: the wire's torsion constant?

presets.label: Constant angular acceleration
presets.description: A disc slows from 120 rad/s to rest in 50 revolutions.

scenarios.title: First-order change
scenarios.description: Decay, growth, or relaxing towards a level: y' = -k (y - level) + source.
scenarios.law: The rate of change is proportional to how far the quantity is from where it is heading.

fields.label: Source rate
fields.hint: How fast the source alone would change the temperature.

fields.label: Source rate
fields.hint: How fast the source alone would change the amount.

fields.label: Source rate
fields.hint: How fast the source alone would change the concentration.

fields.label: Source rate
fields.hint: How fast the source alone would change the voltage.

fields.label: Source rate
fields.hint: How fast the source alone would change the current.

fields.label: Source rate
fields.hint: How fast the source alone would change the speed.

fields.label: Source rate
fields.hint: How fast the source alone would change the population.

fields.label: Source rate
fields.hint: How fast the source alone would change the value.

fields.label: Fraction of the initial difference left (growth: growth factor)
fields.hint: Decay: 0.25 means a quarter is left. Growth: 8 means eight times the start.

effects.label: What is changing?
effects.description: This only sets the names and units of the rows.

effects.label: How it changes
effects.description: Decay towards zero, relax towards a level, or grow.

effects.label: Constant source
effects.description: Something adds to (or removes from) the quantity at a steady rate.

presets.label: Cooling coffee
presets.description: Coffee at 90 °C in a 22 °C room is 75 °C after 5 minutes; when is it 60 °C?

presets.label: Time since death
presets.description: A body at 29.5 °C in an 18 °C room, cooling constant 0.19 per hour.

presets.label: Roast in the oven
presets.description: A 5 °C roast in a 180 °C oven reads 40 °C after 30 minutes; when is it 70 °C?

presets.label: Processor warming up
presets.description: A chip heated at 180 K/min while losing heat to 25 °C air.

presets.label: Carbon dating
presets.description: A sample has 25% of its carbon-14 left; the half-life is 5730 years.

presets.label: Iodine-131 dose
presets.description: 400 MBq of iodine-131 (half-life 8.02 days): how much is left after 30 days?

presets.label: Drug elimination
presets.description: 200 mg of a drug falls to 150 mg in 2 hours; how much is left after 12 hours?

presets.label: Bacteria doubling
presets.description: A culture doubles every 20 minutes; how long from 1000 to a million cells?

scenarios.title: Series circuit
scenarios.description: Resistor, inductor and capacitor in series, with no source, a battery or AC.
scenarios.law: Kirchhoff's voltage law: the voltages around the loop add up to the source voltage.

fields.label: Phase lag of the capacitor voltage
Phase of the current behind the source
Energy in the capacitor at that time
Energy in the inductor at that time
Damping ratio
fields.hint: Below 1 the circuit rings; 1 is critical; above 1 it is overdamped.

effects.label: Resistor
effects.description: A resistance R in the loop.

effects.label: Inductor
effects.description: An inductance L in the loop.

effects.label: Capacitor
effects.description: A capacitance C in the loop.

effects.label: Source
effects.description: What drives the circuit.

effects.label: Internal resistance
effects.description: The source has its own resistance in series.

effects.label: Leaky capacitor
effects.description: A resistance across the capacitor lets charge drain away.
